strict.criterion: AI stocks had a real correction in 2026: a drawdown of at least 20% in the AI leaders, with the S&P 500's concentration in them falling.
strict.measure: Nasdaq-100 or a Magnificent Seven index down at least 20% peak to trough during 2026 per index data or major-outlet reporting, and the top-10 weight of the S&P 500 lower at the latest reading than at the start of the year; provisional until December 31.

standard.criterion: AI stocks corrected in 2026: a drawdown of at least 10% in the AI leaders and underperformance of the broad market for the year.
standard.measure: Magnificent Seven or Nasdaq-100 down at least 10% peak to trough in 2026 and trailing the S&P 500 year to date at the latest reading; provisional.

lenient.criterion: AI stocks had at least one widely reported correction of 10% or more in 2026.
lenient.measure: Nasdaq-100 or a Magnificent Seven index down at least 10% from a 2026 high at some point in the year, per index data or major-outlet reporting.

notes: A heading, so the bars supply the size: 20% is a conventional correction-to-bear threshold, 10% a correction. The China catalyst he names is not graded.

strict.criterion: The US entered a recession in 2026.
strict.measure: An NBER-dated recession beginning in 2026, or two consecutive quarters of negative real GDP in 2026 per the BEA; provisional until the data exists.

standard.criterion: The US economy contracted in 2026: at least one quarter of negative real GDP.
standard.measure: BEA advance or later estimate for any 2026 quarter below zero; provisional.

lenient.criterion: The US economy stalled in 2026: a quarter near zero with rising unemployment, or a recession indicator that triggered.
lenient.measure: A 2026 quarter of real GDP growth below 0.5% annualised with the unemployment rate up at least 0.5 points from its 2026 low, or the Sahm rule triggering in 2026, per BEA and BLS data; provisional.

notes: Split from c1. He hedged with 'likely'; the bars grade the outcome.

strict.criterion: The data-center bubble burst in 2026: large announced build-outs were cancelled or written down and a leading AI-infrastructure company's stock collapsed.
strict.measure: Cancellations, withdrawals or write-downs of announced data-center projects totalling at least $100 billion in 2026 per major-outlet reporting, and at least one leading AI-infrastructure company (Oracle, CoreWeave, Nebius or peers) down 50% or more from its 2025-26 peak at the latest reading; provisional.

standard.criterion: The data-center boom cracked in 2026: multiple large projects were cancelled or delayed and at least one major AI-infrastructure stock fell sharply.
standard.measure: Two or more major-outlet reports of large data-center projects cancelled or delayed in 2026, and at least one AI-infrastructure stock down 30% or more from its peak at the latest reading; provisional.

lenient.criterion: At least one hyperscaler or major financier pulled back on data-center plans in 2026.
lenient.measure: Major-outlet reporting dated 2026 of a cut, pause or cancellation of data-center capex plans by Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Oracle, OpenAI or a major lender.

notes: 'Bursts' is given a size at strict; lenient asks only for a visible pullback.

strict.criterion: Both Nvidia and OpenAI lost material share in 2026.
strict.measure: Reputable 2026 reporting or market data showing Nvidia's AI accelerator share down at least 10 points (to AMD, custom silicon or Chinese chips) and OpenAI losing its lead in enterprise or consumer AI usage to Anthropic or Google; provisional.

standard.criterion: Both Nvidia and OpenAI came under visible competitive siege in 2026, with reputable reporting of share loss for each.
standard.measure: Major-outlet reporting dated 2026 of share loss or pricing pressure at Nvidia and of share loss at OpenAI (enterprise or consumer), one or more reports each.

lenient.criterion: Either Nvidia or OpenAI faced widely reported competitive pressure in 2026.

notes: 'Under siege' is read as share loss at strict and standard, pressure at lenient.

strict.criterion: Amazon was the best-performing Magnificent Seven stock of 2026.
strict.measure: AMZN 2026 year-to-date total return above each of AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, META, NVDA and TSLA at the latest close; provisional until December 31.

standard.criterion: Amazon beat the Magnificent Seven as a group and the S&P 500 in 2026.
standard.measure: AMZN 2026 YTD return above the equal-weighted Mag 7 average and above the S&P 500; provisional.

lenient.measure: AMZN 2026 YTD total return above the S&P 500's; provisional.

notes: 'Big Tech pick' is read as relative performance against the group at strict and standard.

strict.criterion: Space became the next big thing in 2026: a landmark SpaceX capital event and record private space investment.
strict.measure: A SpaceX IPO filing or a transaction valuing it at $1 trillion or more in 2026, and private space investment at a record for the year per Space Capital or a peer tracker; provisional.

standard.criterion: Private space investment set a record in 2026, or SpaceX filed to go public.
standard.measure: Space Capital or peer tracker annual or year-to-date record, or an S-1 filing, dated 2026; provisional.

lenient.criterion: Space investment grew in 2026 or a major space company went public.
lenient.measure: Tracker data showing year-over-year growth, or a space IPO raising $1 billion or more, dated 2026.

notes: The heading names no event; the bars anchor on investment flows and SpaceX, which he singles out.

strict.criterion: The US TikTok stake proved the best investment of 2026: worth more than double the $28 billion deal value within the year.
strict.measure: A transaction, funding round or credible reporting in 2026 valuing the US TikTok joint venture at $60 billion or more; provisional.

standard.criterion: The US TikTok joint venture was valued above the $28 billion deal value in 2026.
standard.measure: A later transaction or credible valuation report in 2026 above $28 billion; provisional.

lenient.criterion: The TikTok US deal closed in 2026 and reporting described the $28 billion price as a bargain for the buyers.
lenient.measure: Deal closing per major outlets, plus at least one major-outlet analysis dated 2026 describing the valuation as below fair value.

notes: 'Best investment' read as the asset's value rising well above the deal price; he gave $28 billion as the deal value, so the bars use it.

strict.criterion: Hollywood took visible damage from short-form video and AI in 2026: a major studio or network made deep cuts citing them, and YouTube's share of TV time passed all subscription streamers combined.
strict.measure: A major studio or network announcing cuts of 20% or more, a shutdown, or a flagship cancellation in 2026 explicitly citing short-form video or AI economics, per major outlets, and Nielsen's Gauge showing YouTube above the combined share of Netflix, Disney+, Prime Video and Max in a 2026 month; provisional.

standard.criterion: At least one major studio or network made cuts or cancelled a flagship show in 2026, citing short-form video or AI economics.
standard.measure: Major-outlet reporting dated 2026 with the attribution in the company's statement or the reporting.

lenient.criterion: In 2026 YouTube or TikTok viewing overtook traditional TV among young audiences, or AI tools were credited with cutting production costs at a major studio.
lenient.measure: Nielsen or a reputable survey dated 2026, or major-outlet reporting of AI-driven cost cuts at a studio.

notes: 'Meteors strike' is read as cuts and share shift. The Colbert example is c9.

strict.criterion: Stephen Colbert launched a podcast or independent digital show in 2026 with a small team.
strict.measure: Launch per major-outlet reporting dated 2026, with a reported team of fewer than 10 people; provisional.

standard.criterion: Stephen Colbert announced or launched a podcast or digital show in 2026.
standard.measure: Announcement or launch per major-outlet reporting dated 2026; provisional.

lenient.criterion: Stephen Colbert signed with a podcast or digital platform, or publicly committed to one, in 2026.

notes: Split from c8. The Late Show ends in May 2026; the dollar figures he gives are illustrative and not graded.

strict.criterion: Waymo dominated in 2026: paid rides at least doubled, it expanded to many more cities, and no rival came close.
strict.measure: Waymo at 2 million or more paid rides a month (from 1 million at the end of 2025) per company statements, operating in at least 10 US metro areas, and at least 5x the paid rides of any other US robotaxi operator at the latest 2026 reading; provisional.

standard.criterion: Waymo's paid rides at least doubled in 2026 and it remained the largest US robotaxi operator.
standard.measure: Company statements or reputable reporting dated 2026; provisional.

lenient.criterion: Waymo remained the largest US robotaxi operator by paid rides in 2026.
lenient.measure: Reputable reporting or company data at the latest 2026 reading; provisional.

notes: 'Dominates' is given a growth and lead definition; he supplied the 1 million rides a month baseline.

strict.criterion: Humanoid robots stayed a demo in 2026: none shipped to paying external customers in volume.
strict.measure: No humanoid robot maker (Tesla, Figure, Agility, Unitree, 1X or peers) reported 1,000 or more units delivered to external paying customers in 2026, per company statements or major outlets; provisional.

standard.criterion: Tesla's Optimus was not sold to external customers in 2026.
standard.measure: No external Optimus sales reported by Tesla or major outlets in 2026; provisional.

lenient.criterion: Tesla missed its own stated 2026 Optimus production or sales targets.
lenient.measure: Tesla's stated 2026 targets versus reported output, per company statements or major-outlet reporting dated 2026; provisional.

notes: The analogy to 2015 self-driving is read as 'hype ahead of product'. Industrial robots are out of scope.

strict.criterion: Prediction markets were the vice of 2026: volume at least doubled, the gaming stocks he named trailed the market, and the gambling and addiction framing was widespread.
strict.measure: Combined Kalshi and Polymarket 2026 volume at least 2x 2025 (annualised); the six named gaming stocks (Aristocrat, Caesars, DraftKings, Evolution, Flutter, MGM) on average underperforming the S&P 500 in 2026; and two or more major outlets framing prediction markets as gambling or addiction in 2026; provisional.

standard.criterion: Prediction markets grew strongly in 2026 and were widely framed as gambling, with legal or regulatory challenges.
standard.measure: Volume up at least 50% on 2025 (annualised) per Dune or The Block, plus major-outlet framing and at least one state or federal legal action dated 2026.

lenient.criterion: Prediction markets were a widely covered backlash or addiction topic in 2026.
lenient.measure: Two or more major outlets dated 2026.

notes: 'Vice of the year' is read as growth plus backlash; the gaming-stock clause is required only at strict.

strict.criterion: Synthetic relationships took center stage in 2026: AI companions became a national policy issue with binding rules, while usage kept growing.
strict.measure: A federal law or FTC rule on AI companions enacted or finalised in 2026, or companion-chatbot laws enacted in at least three states in 2026, plus reported growth in companion usage (Character.ai, Replika, ChatGPT companion features); provisional.

standard.criterion: AI companions became a major public and policy issue in 2026.
standard.measure: State laws, lawsuits, congressional hearings or an FTC action on AI companions dated 2026, per major-outlet reporting, two or more such events.

lenient.criterion: AI companion harms to young people were a widely covered topic in 2026.
lenient.measure: Two or more major outlets dated 2026.

notes: 'Center stage' is read as policy action at strict and standard, coverage at lenient. The 'next opioid crisis' line is rhetoric and not graded.

strict.criterion: The 'college is dead' narrative collapsed in 2026: enrollment rose again and the reversal was widely reported.
strict.measure: National Student Clearinghouse fall 2026 (or latest 2026) undergraduate enrollment up year over year, plus major-outlet reporting dated 2026 describing the narrative as wrong or reversing; provisional.

standard.measure: National Student Clearinghouse spring or fall 2026 report showing year-over-year growth; provisional.

lenient.criterion: US undergraduate enrollment held steady or rose in 2026.
lenient.measure: National Student Clearinghouse 2026 report, flat or up year over year; provisional.

notes: The degree-premium argument is background; the bars grade enrollment, which is the measurable claim he made.

strict.criterion: Scotland reached the semifinals of the 2026 World Cup.

standard.criterion: Scotland reached the semifinals of the 2026 World Cup.

lenient.criterion: Scotland reached the semifinals of the 2026 World Cup.

notes: Binary; identical bars. He flagged it as a dream. The McTominay clause is not graded.
